```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# read NAO data
nao <- read_csv(paste0(home, "/data/env/NAO data - extended time series.csv")) |>
  dplyr::rename(year = Year)

nao <- nao |>
  arrange(year) |>
  mutate(
    nao = slide_dbl(winter_NAO, mean, .before = 4, .complete = TRUE)
  )

nao |>
  pivot_longer(c("nao", "winter_NAO")) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, value, color = name)) +
  geom_line()

mid_year <- round(median(1959:2022))

d <- dat |>
  mutate(
    species_f = as.factor(Species),
    stock_f = as.factor(stock),
    year_ct = year - mid_year
  ) |>
  group_by(stock_f, species_f) |>
  arrange(year, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    sst_lag1      = lag(sst, 1),
    salinity_lag1 = lag(salinity, 1)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  # Filter to analysis period BEFORE scaling
  filter(year >= 1959) |>
  left_join(nao, by = "year") |>
  # Scale within stock (mean and SD), matching how the response is scaled
  mutate(
    sst_sc_lag1       = (sst_lag1 - mean(sst_lag1, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(sst_lag1, na.rm = TRUE),
    salinity_sc_lag1  = (salinity_lag1 - mean(salinity_lag1, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(salinity_lag1, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = stock_f
  ) |>
  # NAO is a single time series common to all stocks; scale globally
  mutate(
    nao_sc = as.numeric(scale(nao))
  ) |>
  # Scale response within stock
  mutate(
    b0_sc = (b0 - mean(b0, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(b0, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = stock_f
  ) |>
  tidylog::drop_na(b0_sc) |>
  tidylog::drop_na(sst_sc_lag1) |>
  tidylog::drop_na(salinity_sc_lag1) |>
  tidylog::drop_na(nao_sc) |>
  droplevels()


d |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(sst_sc_lag1, salinity_sc_lag1),
    names_to = "covariate", values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  mutate(var = str_remove(covariate, "_sc_lag1")) |>
  ggplot(aes(value, b0_sc)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, k = 3), se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~var, scales = "free_x") +
  guides(color = "none") +
  labs(x = "Scaled predictor (1-year lag, within-stock scaled)", y = "B0 (scaled)")
```

## Fit model

```{r}
m_test <- brms::brm(
  b0_sc ~
    s(year_ct) +
    sst_sc_lag1 + salinity_sc_lag1 + nao_sc +
    (1 + sst_sc_lag1 + salinity_sc_lag1 | stock_f) +
    (1 | species_f),
  family = brms::student(link = "identity", link_sigma = "log", link_nu = "logm1"),
  data = d,
  chains = 1,
  iter = 1,
  cores = 1
)

prior_summary(m_test)

priors <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 5), class = "b"),
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 2.5), class = "Intercept"),
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 2.5), class = "sds"),
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 2.5), class = "sd"),
  prior(lkj_corr_cholesky(1), class = "cor"),
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 2.5), class = "sigma"),
  prior(gamma(2, 0.1), class = "nu")
)
```

```{r}
# s(year_ct): global nonlinear trend over time. It captures long-term trajectories not tied to interannual covariate fluctuation.
# sst_sc_lag1 + salinity_sc_lag1: stock-centered, 1-year-lagged environmental covariates. Random slopes on stock_f = stock-specific sensitivity.
# nao_sc: 5-year sliding mean NAO; fixed only, operates at too broad a scale for stock-specific responses to be identifiable.
# (1|species_f): variation in mean B0 among species

priors_gauss <- priors
priors_gauss <- priors[priors$class != "nu", ]

priors_skewb <- priors_skew[priors_skew$class != "cor", ]

m2b <- brms::brm(
  b0_sc ~
    s(year_ct) +
    sst_sc_lag1 + salinity_sc_lag1 + nao_sc +
    (1 + sst_sc_lag1 + salinity_sc_lag1 || stock_f) +
    (1 | species_f),
  family = "skew_normal",
  data = d,
  sample_prior = "yes",
  control = list(max_treedepth = 12,
                 adapt_delta = 0.99),
  prior = priors_skewb,
  chains = 5,
  iter = 5000,

)
```

## Prior vs posterior

```{r}
post <- as_draws_df(m2b)

# Fixed effects
fixed_post <- bind_rows(
  tibble(parameter = "sst", value = post$b_sst_sc_lag1),
  tibble(parameter = "salinity", value = post$b_salinity_sc_lag1),
  tibble(parameter = "nao", value = post$b_nao_sc)
) |>
  mutate(distribution = "Posterior", group = "Fixed effects")

fixed_prior <- crossing(
  parameter = unique(fixed_post$parameter),
  value = post$prior_b
) |>
  mutate(distribution = "Prior", group = "Fixed effects")

# Random-effect SDs
sd_post <- bind_rows(
  tibble(parameter = "stock", value = post$sd_stock_f__Intercept),
  tibble(parameter = "species", value = post$sd_species_f__Intercept)
) |>
  mutate(distribution = "Posterior", group = "Random-effect SD")

sd_prior <- bind_rows(
  tibble(parameter = "stock", value = post$prior_sd_stock_f),
  tibble(parameter = "species", value = post$prior_sd_species_f)
) |>
  mutate(distribution = "Prior", group = "Random-effect SD")

# Sigma
sigma_dat <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    parameter = "sigma", value = post$prior_sigma,
    distribution = "Prior", group = "Residual SD"
  ),
  tibble(
    parameter = "sigma", value = post$sigma,
    distribution = "Posterior", group = "Residual SD"
  )
)

# Alpha (skewness)
alpha_dat <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    parameter = "alpha", value = post$prior_alpha,
    distribution = "Prior", group = "Skewness"
  ),
  tibble(
    parameter = "alpha", value = post$alpha,
    distribution = "Posterior", group = "Skewness"
  )
)

# Combine
plot_dat <- bind_rows(fixed_post, fixed_prior, sd_post, sd_prior, sigma_dat, alpha_dat) |>
  mutate(
    parameter = factor(
      parameter,
      levels = c(
        "sst", "salinity", "nao",
        "stock", "species", "sigma", "alpha"
      )
    )
  )

# Crop to posterior range
limits <- plot_dat |>
  group_by(parameter) |>
  summarise(
    lower = quantile(value[distribution == "Posterior"], 0.001) - 0.5,
    upper = quantile(value[distribution == "Posterior"], 0.999) + 0.5,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

plot_dat_crop <- plot_dat |>
  left_join(limits, by = "parameter") |>
  filter(between(value, lower, upper)) |>
  select(-lower, -upper)

ggplot(plot_dat_crop, aes(x = value, fill = distribution, colour = distribution)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.4, trim = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free", ncol = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Prior = "grey85", Posterior = "steelblue")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Prior = "grey40", Posterior = NA)) +
  guides(colour = "none", fill = guide_legend(position = "inside")) +
  labs(x = "Parameter value", y = "Density") +
  coord_cartesian(expand = 0) +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.position.inside = c(0.055, 0.95),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

ggsave(paste0(home, "/figures/supp/prior_posterior_comparison.pdf"),
  width = 20, height = 17, units = "cm"
)
```

## Plot random intercepts

```{r}
posterior_epred(m2b) |>
  t() |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(stock_f = d$stock_f) |>
  pivot_longer(-stock_f, names_to = "draw", values_to = "pred") |>
  group_by(stock_f, draw) |>
  summarise(stock_mean = mean(pred), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(stock_f) |>
  median_qi(stock_mean, .width = 0.5) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    y = reorder(stock_f, stock_mean), x = stock_mean,
    xmin = .lower, xmax = .upper
  )) +
  geom_pointinterval(alpha = 0.75, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(x = expression(paste("Mean predicted ", B[0], " (scaled)")), y = "Stock")

# Stock random effects
m2b |>
  spread_draws(b_Intercept, r_stock_f[stock_f, term]) |>
  filter(term == "Intercept") |>
  mutate(stock_mean = b_Intercept + r_stock_f) |>
  median_qi(stock_mean, .width = 0.5) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    y = reorder(stock_f, stock_mean), x = stock_mean,
    xmin = .lower, xmax = .upper
  )) +
  geom_pointinterval(alpha = 0.75, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    x = "Random effect (stock intercept)",
    y = "Stock"
  )

# ggsave(paste0(home, "/figures/supp/stock_re.pdf"),
#   width = 20, height = 17, units = "cm"
# )

# Species random effects
m2b |>
  spread_draws(b_Intercept, r_species_f[species_f, term]) |>
  filter(term == "Intercept") |>
  mutate(species_mean = b_Intercept + r_species_f) |>
  median_qi(species_mean, .width = 0.5) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    y = reorder(species_f, species_mean), x = species_mean,
    xmin = .lower, xmax = .upper
  )) +
  geom_pointinterval(alpha = 0.75, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    x = expression(paste("Predicted ", B[0], " (scaled)")),
    y = "Species"
  )

#   width = 20, height = 17, units = "cm"
# )
```

## Main effects

```{r}
# Fixed effects
fixed_draws <- m2b |>
  gather_draws(
    b_sst_sc_lag1, b_salinity_sc_lag1, b_nao_sc
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    var = forcats::fct_recode(
      .variable,
      "SST (deviation)"      = "b_sst_sc_lag1",
      "Salinity (deviation)" = "b_salinity_sc_lag1",
      "NAO"                  = "b_nao_sc"
    ),
    panel = "Fixed effects"
  )

# Random SDs
sd_draws <- m2b |>
  gather_draws(
    sd_stock_f__Intercept, sd_stock_f__sst_sc_lag1,
    sd_stock_f__salinity_sc_lag1,
    sd_species_f__Intercept
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    var = forcats::fct_recode(
      .variable,
      "Stock (intercept)"   = "sd_stock_f__Intercept",
      "Stock (SST)"         = "sd_stock_f__sst_sc_lag1",
      "Stock (Salinity)"    = "sd_stock_f__salinity_sc_lag1",
      "Species (intercept)" = "sd_species_f__Intercept"
    ),
    panel = "Random effect SDs"
  )

# Combine and plot
bind_rows(fixed_draws, sd_draws) |>
  mutate(
    var = forcats::fct_reorder(var, .value, .fun = median),
    panel = factor(panel, levels = c("Fixed effects", "Random effect SDs"))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = var, x = .value, fill = panel)) +
  stat_halfeye(alpha = 0.35) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("forestgreen", "steelblue")) +
  geom_vline(
    data = ~ filter(.x, panel == "Fixed effects"),
    aes(xintercept = 0), linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Estimate") +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  theme(
    plot.margin = margin(c(0, 0.3, 0, 0.1), unit = "cm"),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank()
  )

ggsave(paste0(home, "/figures/supp/pars.pdf"), width = 17, height = 12, units = "cm")
```

## Plot random slopes

```{r}
# get_variables(m2b)

re_long <- m2b |>
  spread_draws(
    b_sst_sc_lag1, b_salinity_sc_lag1,
    r_stock_f[stock_f, term]
  ) |>
  filter(term %in% c("sst_sc_lag1", "salinity_sc_lag1")) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    fixed_effect = case_when(
      term == "sst_sc_lag1" ~ b_sst_sc_lag1,
      term == "salinity_sc_lag1" ~ b_salinity_sc_lag1
    ),
    total_slope = fixed_effect + r_stock_f
  ) |>
  group_by(stock_f, term) |>
  median_qi(total_slope, fixed_effect, .width = 0.95) |>
  mutate(
    sig = case_when(
      total_slope.lower > 0 ~ "Positive sig.",
      total_slope.upper < 0 ~ "Negative sig.",
      TRUE ~ "No effect"
    ),
    covariate = term
  )

# Facet
re_long <- re_long |>
  mutate(
    covariate = recode(covariate,
      "sst_sc_lag1"      = "SST",
      "salinity_sc_lag1" = "Salinity"
    ),
    covariate = factor(covariate, levels = c("SST", "Salinity"))
  )

# Count signs by term
re_summary <- re_long |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    covariate = recode(covariate,
      "sst_sc_lag1"      = "SST",
      "salinity_sc_lag1" = "Salinity"
    ),
    covariate = factor(covariate, levels = c("SST", "Salinity"))
  ) |>
  summarise(n = n(), .by = c(sig, covariate)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sig, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(
    tot = `Negative sig.` + `No effect` + `Positive sig.`,
    neg_prop = paste0(round((`Negative sig.` / tot)*100, digits = 1), "%"),
    no_prop = paste0(round((`No effect` / tot)*100, digits = 1), "%"),
    pos_prop = paste0(round((`Positive sig.` / tot)*100, digits = 1), "%")
  )

re_summary |> as.data.frame()

# Plot
re_long |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_text(
    data = re_summary,
    aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = pos_prop),
    hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.25, inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "steelblue", size = 3
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = re_summary,
    aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = no_prop),
    hjust = 1.1, vjust = 2.5, inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "grey70", size = 3
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = re_summary,
    aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = neg_prop),
    hjust = 1.1, vjust = 3.75, inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "tomato", size = 3
  ) +
  geom_errorbarh(
    aes(
      y = stock_f,
      xmin = total_slope.lower,
      xmax = total_slope.upper,
      color = sig
    ),
    height = 0
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(
      y = stock_f,
      x = total_slope,
      color = sig
    ),
    size = 2
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_rect(
    data = re_long |>
      group_by(covariate) |>
      summarise(
        xmin = unique(fixed_effect.lower),
        xmax = unique(fixed_effect.upper),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
    fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.25, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Positive sig." = "steelblue",
    "Negative sig." = "tomato",
    "No effect"     = "grey70"
  )) +
  facet_wrap(~covariate, ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = "Total slope (fixed + random)", y = NULL) +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.background = element_blank()
  )

ggsave(paste0(home, "/figures/supp/stock_slopes.pdf"), width = 20, height = 23, units = "cm")
```

## Plot year effect

```{r}
p2
```

## Year effects by stock!

```{r}
# Get per-stock mean and SD of b0 for back-transformation, matching how
# b0_sc is actually built (z-scored within stock, on the raw scale)
stock_scale <- d |>
  summarise(
    mean_b0 = mean(b0, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_b0 = sd(b0, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = stock_f
  )

## Actual declines in b0 (percentage), with posterior uncertainty
# ML: 1996 is the anchor year for the long-run comparison, not 1960: 68 of 79
# stocks don't have predictions back to 1960 (some start as late as 2003), so
# which.min(abs(year - 1960)) would silently pick each stock's own start year
# instead of 1960. 1996 is close to the latest year at which the comparison
# still includes the large majority of stocks (75 of 79); the remaining 4
# (lin.27.5b, ple.27.21-23, whg.27.7b-ce-k, pil.27.8abd) are excluded below.
stock_min_year <- d |>
  summarise(min_year = min(year), .by = stock_f)

stocks_since_1996 <- stock_min_year |>
  filter(min_year <= 1996) |>
  pull(stock_f)

# ML: group_by(stock_f, .draw) BEFORE picking the year-1996/2020 rows, since
# pm_smooth_with_re has 5000 draws per stock-year; without grouping by .draw,
# which.min() just grabs whichever row happens to come first (one arbitrary
# draw), not a proper summary across the posterior.
pct_data <- bind_rows(
  pm_smooth_with_re |>
    filter(stock_f %in% stocks_since_1996) |>
    left_join(stock_scale, by = "stock_f") |>
    mutate(b0_raw = .epred * sd_b0 + mean_b0) |>
    group_by(stock_f, .draw) |>
    summarise(
      b0_ref = b0_raw[which.min(abs(year - 1996))],
      b0_new = b0_raw[which.min(abs(year - 2020))],
      pct_change = (b0_new - b0_ref) / b0_ref * 100,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    group_by(stock_f) |>
    median_qi(pct_change, .width = 0.95) |>
    mutate(comparison = "2020 vs 1996"),
  pm_smooth_with_re |>
    left_join(stock_scale, by = "stock_f") |>
    mutate(b0_raw = .epred * sd_b0 + mean_b0) |>
    group_by(stock_f, .draw) |>
    summarise(
      b0_ref = b0_raw[which.min(abs(year - 2000))],
      b0_new = b0_raw[which.min(abs(year - 2020))],
      pct_change = (b0_new - b0_ref) / b0_ref * 100,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    group_by(stock_f) |>
    median_qi(pct_change, .width = 0.95) |>
    mutate(comparison = "2020 vs 2000")
)

# ML: Order stocks once, by the "2020 vs 1996" point estimate, and reuse that
# same order for both facets so the same stock lines up across panels.
stock_order <- pct_data |>
  filter(comparison == "2020 vs 1996") |>
  arrange(desc(pct_change)) |>
  pull(stock_f)

pp_dat <- pct_data |>
  mutate(
    direction = ifelse(pct_change < 0, "Decline", "Increase"),
    stock_f = factor(stock_f, levels = stock_order)
  ) |>
  group_by(comparison) |>
  mutate(
    n_neg = sum(pct_change < 0),
    n_pos = sum(pct_change >= 0),
    n_tot = n(),
    label_neg = paste0(round(n_neg / n_tot * 100), "%\ndeclining"),
    label_pos = paste0(round(n_pos / n_tot * 100), "%\nincreasing")
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  tidylog::filter(between(pct_change, -500, 500))

# Per-stock, per-draw % change (before collapsing to per-stock summaries)
pct_draws_1996 <- pm_smooth_with_re |>
  filter(stock_f %in% stocks_since_1996) |>
  left_join(stock_scale, by = "stock_f") |>
  mutate(b0_raw = .epred * sd_b0 + mean_b0) |>
  group_by(stock_f, .draw) |>
  summarise(
    b0_ref = b0_raw[which.min(abs(year - 1996))],
    b0_new = b0_raw[which.min(abs(year - 2020))],
    pct_change = (b0_new - b0_ref) / b0_ref * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# For each draw, summarise across stocks first, then take the posterior
# median and 95% CI of that across-stock summary -- this is the overall
# central tendency with genuine posterior uncertainty, not just the spread
# of the per-stock point estimates.
overall_summary_1996 <- pct_draws_1996 |>
  group_by(.draw) |>
  summarise(
    mean_pct = mean(pct_change),
    median_pct = median(pct_change),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(c(mean_pct, median_pct), names_to = "stat", values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(stat) |>
  median_qi(value, .width = 0.95)

overall_label <- paste0(
  "Mean: ", round(overall_summary_1996$value[overall_summary_1996$stat == "mean_pct"], 1), "% ",
  "[", round(overall_summary_1996$.lower[overall_summary_1996$stat == "mean_pct"], 1), ", ",
  round(overall_summary_1996$.upper[overall_summary_1996$stat == "mean_pct"], 1), "]\n",
  "Median: ", round(overall_summary_1996$value[overall_summary_1996$stat == "median_pct"], 1), "% ",
  "[", round(overall_summary_1996$.lower[overall_summary_1996$stat == "median_pct"], 1), ", ",
  round(overall_summary_1996$.upper[overall_summary_1996$stat == "median_pct"], 1), "]"
)

pp <- pp_dat |>
  filter(comparison == "2020 vs 1996") |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = pct_change, y = stock_f,
    xmin = .lower, xmax = .upper,
    color = direction
  )) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
  geom_pointinterval(size = 0.3, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(
    data = distinct(pp_dat, comparison, label_neg) |>
      filter(comparison == "2020 vs 1996"),
    aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = label_neg),
    hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.25, inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "tomato2", size = 3
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = distinct(pp_dat, comparison, label_pos) |>
      filter(comparison == "2020 vs 1996"),
    aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = label_pos),
    hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.25, inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "steelblue", size = 3
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text", x = -Inf, y = -Inf, label = overall_label,
    hjust = -0.05, vjust = -0.3, size = 3, color = "grey20"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Decline" = "tomato2", "Increase" = "steelblue")) +
  facet_wrap(~comparison, ncol = 2, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "% change in B0 (median, 95% CI)", y = NULL) +
  guides(color = "none") +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_blank()
  )

pp

ggsave(paste0(home, "/figures/stock_trends_pct.pdf"),
  width = 19, height = 21, units = "cm"
)

# Plot trends by stock, color by temperature slope
p1 <- pm_smooth_with_re |>
  left_join(
    re_long |>

p1
```

## Anything common in the declining / increasing species?

```{r}
# Seems that the divergence in last years is linked to temperature slope. So what is linked to the temperature slope then? Is it life history, thermal niche, or what? Try some cluster analysis?
library(icesdata)

out <- names(icesdata) |>
  map(function(stock_name) {
    stk <- icesdata[[stock_name]]
    fl <- attributes(stk)$fishlife
    if (is.null(fl)) {
      return(NULL)
    }

    tibble(
      stock_f = stock_name,
      species = attributes(stk)$species,
      linf = unname(fl["linf"]),
      k = unname(fl["k"]),
      age_maturity = mean(as.numeric(mat50(stk)), na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  }) |>
  list_rbind()

stock_trends <- pm_smooth_with_re |>
  filter(year >= 1990) |>
  dplyr::group_by(stock_f, year) |>
  dplyr::summarise(.epred = median(.epred), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::group_by(stock_f) |>
  dplyr::summarise(trend = coef(lm(.epred ~ year))[2], .groups = "drop")

mean_sst <- dat |>
  dplyr::rename(stock_f = stock) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    sst = mean(sst),
    .by = stock_f
  )

stock_trends_traits <- stock_trends |>
  left_join(out, by = "stock_f")

stock_trends_traits |>
  pivot_longer(c(linf, k, age_maturity)) |>
  ggplot(aes(value, trend)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = stock_f), size = 2, color = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3) +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +
  labs(y = expression(paste("Trend in predicted ", B[0], " (2000-present)")), x = NULL)

re_long |>
  filter(term == "sst_sc_lag1") |>
  left_join(out, by = "stock_f") |>
  pivot_longer(c(linf, k, age_maturity)) |>
  ggplot(aes(value, total_slope)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_x")
```

## Alternative model without year smooth

```{r}
# ML: No population-level smooth here, so instead each stock gets its own
# linear year trend (fixed year_ct + stock-specific random slope). This
# gives stock-specific secular drift (assessment changes, selectivity, or
# anything else slowly varying over time that isn't temperature) somewhere
# to go other than the SST/salinity random slopes, since year and SST are
# substantially collinear within most stocks (median within-stock
# cor(year, sst_sc_lag1) = 0.65, 76 of 79 stocks > 0.5). If the SST/salinity
# slopes and the pct_change-vs-SST-slope relationship hold up once year_ct
# is explicitly modeled per stock, that's evidence they aren't just picking
# up generic non-temperature trend.
priors_ns <- priors_skewb |> filter(class != "sds")

m2b_ns <- brms::brm(
  b0_sc ~
    year_ct + sst_sc_lag1 + salinity_sc_lag1 + nao_sc +
    (1 + year_ct + sst_sc_lag1 + salinity_sc_lag1 || stock_f) +
    (1 | species_f),
  family = "skew_normal",
  data = d,
  sample_prior = "yes",
  prior = priors_ns,
  control = list(
    adapt_delta = 0.99,
    max_treedepth = 12
  ),
  chains = 5,
  iter = 5000,
  cores = 5
)

saveRDS(m2b_ns, paste0(home, "/output/m2b_ns.rds"))

m2b_ns <- readRDS(paste0(home, "/output/m2b_ns.rds"))

loo(m2b, m2b_ns)

# Compare effects
model_list <- list(
  "With year smooth"    = list(mod = m2b, suffix = "_lag1"),
  "Without year smooth" = list(mod = m2b_ns, suffix = "_lag1")
)

fixed_draws_multi <- purrr::imap_dfr(model_list, function(x, mod_name) {
  mod <- x$mod
  suffix <- x$suffix

  mod |>
    gather_draws(
      !!sym(paste0("b_sst_sc", suffix)),
      !!sym(paste0("b_salinity_sc", suffix)),
      b_nao_sc
    ) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(
      var = case_when(
        str_detect(.variable, "sst") ~ "SST",
        str_detect(.variable, "salinity") ~ "Salinity",
        str_detect(.variable, "nao") ~ "NAO"
      ),
      model = mod_name
    )
})

fixed_draws_multi |>
  mutate(
    var   = forcats::fct_reorder(var, .value, .fun = median),
    model = factor(model, levels = c("With year smooth", "Without year smooth"))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = model, x = .value, fill = model, color = model)) +
  stat_halfeye(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~var, scales = "free_x", ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Estimate", fill = "Model", color = "Model") +
  guides(fill = "none", color = "none") +
  theme(
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank()
  )

r2_bayes(m2b_ns)
```

## Does the SST attribution survive an explicit per-stock year trend?

```{r}
# ML: pct_data (comparison == "2020 vs 1996") and re_long were already built
# earlier from m2b. Build the same two quantities from m2b_ns (which has an
# explicit year_ct fixed + random slope per stock) and compare.
pm_smooth_with_re_ns <- d |>
  tidylog::drop_na() |>
  tidylog::filter(year >= 1959) |>
  add_epred_draws(m2b_ns, ndraws = 5000, seed = 42)

pct_data_ns_1996 <- pm_smooth_with_re_ns |>
  filter(stock_f %in% stocks_since_1996) |>
  left_join(stock_scale, by = "stock_f") |>
  mutate(b0_raw = .epred * sd_b0 + mean_b0) |>
  group_by(stock_f, .draw) |>
  summarise(
    b0_ref = b0_raw[which.min(abs(year - 1996))],
    b0_new = b0_raw[which.min(abs(year - 2020))],
    pct_change = (b0_new - b0_ref) / b0_ref * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  group_by(stock_f) |>
  median_qi(pct_change, .width = 0.95) |>
  mutate(stock_f = as.character(stock_f)) |>
  select(stock_f, pct_change)

re_long_ns <- m2b_ns |>
  spread_draws(b_sst_sc_lag1, r_stock_f[stock_f, term]) |>
  filter(term == "sst_sc_lag1") |>
  mutate(total_slope = b_sst_sc_lag1 + r_stock_f) |>
  group_by(stock_f) |>
  median_qi(total_slope, .width = 0.95) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(stock_f = as.character(stock_f)) |>
  select(stock_f, sst_total_slope = total_slope)

# Original (m2b, with s(year_ct)) for comparison
pct_data_orig_1996 <- pct_data |>
  filter(comparison == "2020 vs 1996") |>
  select(stock_f, pct_change) |>
  mutate(stock_f = as.character(stock_f))

re_long_orig <- re_long |>
  filter(term == "sst_sc_lag1") |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(stock_f = as.character(stock_f)) |>
  select(stock_f, sst_total_slope = total_slope)

fit_orig <- lm(pct_change ~ sst_total_slope, data = left_join(pct_data_orig_1996, re_long_orig, by = "stock_f"))
fit_ns   <- lm(pct_change ~ sst_total_slope, data = left_join(pct_data_ns_1996, re_long_ns, by = "stock_f"))

cat("R2, original m2b (s(year_ct)):", round(summary(fit_orig)$r.squared, 3), "\n")
cat("R2, m2b_ns (explicit per-stock year trend):", round(summary(fit_ns)$r.squared, 3), "\n")

slope_compare <- re_long_orig |>
  dplyr::rename(slope_orig = sst_total_slope) |>
  left_join(re_long_ns |> dplyr::rename(slope_yt = sst_total_slope), by = "stock_f") |>
  drop_na()

cat("Correlation between original and year-trend-adjusted SST slopes: r =",
    round(cor(slope_compare$slope_orig, slope_compare$slope_yt), 3), "\n")
cat("Mean |slope|, original:      ", round(mean(abs(slope_compare$slope_orig)), 3), "\n")
cat("Mean |slope|, year-adjusted: ", round(mean(abs(slope_compare$slope_yt)), 3), "\n")

ggplot(slope_compare, aes(slope_orig, slope_yt)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(
    x = "Total SST slope, m2b (s(year_ct))",
    y = "Total SST slope, m2b_ns (per-stock year trend)"
  )

ggsave(paste0(home, "/figures/supp/sst_slope_yeartrend_check.pdf"), width = 12, height = 10, units = "cm")
```
